title: Personhood of the Holy Spirit
definition: The personhood of the Holy Spirit is the doctrine that the Holy Spirit is a divine Person, not an impersonal force.
summary: The Holy Spirit is not an impersonal power but a divine Person who speaks, leads, teaches, convicts, and can be grieved.
christFocus: Jesus promised the Holy Spirit as another Helper who would teach, guide, glorify Christ, and dwell with believers.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Holy Spirit is not a vague influence or spiritual energy. Scripture speaks of the Spirit as one who teaches, guides, wills, speaks, intercedes, convicts, comforts, and can be grieved. These are personal actions, not the actions of an impersonal force.

The Spirit's personhood matters because believers relate to Him in faith, dependence, reverence, and obedience. He is not something to manipulate or use; He is God present with His people.

Jesus promised the Spirit as another Helper. The Spirit comes to glorify Christ, apply the Gospel, strengthen believers, and lead God's people in truth.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people speak of the Spirit as a feeling, force, or spiritual atmosphere. This doctrine matters because it protects believers from treating the Holy Spirit impersonally and teaches them to depend on Him reverently.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Honor the Holy Spirit as the divine Helper promised by Christ. Seek His help in prayer, obedience, understanding Scripture, resisting sin, and bearing witness to Jesus.
